subject: history_social
passage: Cities of the Indus civilization, which flourished from about 2600 to 1900 BCE in what is now Pakistan and northwestern India, were often hundreds of kilometers apart. Yet builders in many of them used bricks of the same proportions: in each brick, the width was twice the thickness, and the length was twice the width. Because the Indus script has not been deciphered, no written rules for brickmaking are known. Even so, the matching proportions suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: all bricks used in Indus cities were made in a single central workshop.
choices.B: builders in widely separated cities followed common building practices.
choices.C: the Indus script was used mainly to record rules for making bricks.
choices.D: the cities were built by unrelated groups with no contact with one another.

explanation.why: Builders in cities hundreds of kilometers apart made bricks with the same proportions. Even without written rules, this shared pattern points to shared practices across the civilization.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This goes too far: matching proportions show a shared standard, not that every brick came from one workshop.
explanation.B: Correct. The same brick proportions in distant cities point to shared building practices, even though no written rules survive.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The script has not been deciphered, so nothing is known about what it mainly recorded.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This reverses the evidence: identical proportions in distant cities suggest connection, not isolation.
